summary: Brush Hill, Sherborn MA: a 40-ft municipal wooden tower first operated 1920 and used until 1940; a 2014 trail guide shows communications towers on the summit.

facts.status_note: Register lists it as a former site with use ending in 1940; no source describes the structure today

visit.trail_note: 2014 Bay Circuit Trail guide routes walkers southeast through Sherborn Town Forest and up a gravel service road to the summit of Brush Hill

corrections.why: The register describes a 40-foot wooden tower on Brush Hill.

notes_for_editor: Only one register entry gives the tower's dates; no build date, builder, staffing or removal record was found. The 'gone' status rests on the register's former-site listing and the 1940 end date; no source says the tower was taken down. The 2014 Bay Circuit guide describes the Brush Hill summit as having communications towers, but it does not say whether that summit is the lookout's exact site. Access is left out: no source says whether the summit is open to the public. Searches found no newspaper, State Forester or town record of the tower. Next checks: Massachusetts State Forester annual reports from 1920 to 1940, and the Sherborn Historical Society for a build date and removal. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the 2014 guide also mentions an unnamed 'tower site' on a different stretch near Rte 27 (waypoint C, about 1.2 km east of the register point); no source ties it to the lookout. The story now says the guide does not say whether the summit is the lookout's site.
